children: Shares of Dixon Technologies rose nearly 3 percent to an intraday high of Rs 13,215 apiece after the electronic manufacturer announced an agreement to acquire manufacturing assets worth up to Rs 49.75 crore from Vimal Plast (India) Pvt. Ltd to expand its semi-automatic washing machine business.

The stock opened at Rs 12,860.20 and rallied 2.8 percent to touch an intra-day high of Rs 13,221, on the BSE, compared with its previous close of Rs 12,860. At the close of the session, Dixon Technologies shares settled 1.87 percent higher at Rs 13,100.
Dixon Technologies signs Rs 49.75 crore asset deal with Vimal Plast

The buying interest in Dixon Technologies came after the company announced it had signed an asset purchase agreement to acquire manufacturing assets worth up to Rs 49.75 crore from Vimal Plast (India) Pvt. Ltd, according to an exchange filing released on Monday post-market hours.

Under the agreement, Dixon Technologies will acquire moulds, research and development laboratory equipment, Korean basket assembly machines, jigs and fixtures, subject to the fulfilment of specified conditions.

The acquisition aims to strengthen the company’s semi-automatic washing machine original design manufacturing (ODM) capabilities, expand production capacity and deepen relationships with marquee customers, said Atul B. Lall, Vice Chairman and Managing Director of Dixon Technologies (India) Limited.

“The acquisition will enhance our semi-automatic washing machine- ODM capabilities and enable us to deepen our engagement with marquee anchor customers, thereby increasing our wallet share through a broader product portfolio and greater manufacturing capabilities. It will also strengthen our position in the outsourced semi-automatic washing machine segment and enhance our overall share in the Indian washing machine market,” Lall said.

“The integration of these assets with our existing manufacturing ecosystem is expected to improve capacity utilisation, drive operational efficiencies and provide greater economies of scale,” Lall further stated.

Additionally, the acquired moulds, R&D laboratory equipment, specialised machinery and technical infrastructure will strengthen the company’s product development, engineering and design capabilities, enabling us to respond more effectively to evolving customer requirements and accelerating new product introductions, he said.

Lall said the acquisition would further consolidate Dixon Technologies' position as a leading washing machine ODM in India, deepen strategic customer relationships and create a stronger platform for sustainable and profitable growth.

Shares of Dixon Technologies have gained 4 percent in the last week while they have advanced 6.17 percent in one month and 19.32 in six months. The stock, however, has declined 6.76 percent in six months and 16.24 in one year, respectively, according to BSE analytics.
